name: Uncertainty arising AFTER revenue was recognised
definition: When the uncertainty relating to collectability arises subsequent to the time of sale or the rendering of the service, AS 9 states it is more appropriate to make a separate provision to reflect the uncertainty rather than to adjust the amount of revenue originally recorded.
why_it_exists: Doubt has two different answers depending on WHEN it arose, and the difference is the whole point. Doubt existing at the time of the claim stops revenue from being recognised at all (ACC-REV-POSTPONE-001). Doubt arriving later leaves the original revenue alone and creates a provision instead — because at the moment of recognition the revenue was correctly recognised, and rewriting it would misstate a period that was right when it closed.
inputs: the date revenue was originally recognised
the date the uncertainty about collectability arose
the amount originally recorded as revenue
outputs: a separate provision reflecting the uncertainty
preconditions: revenue was already recognised under AS 9
the uncertainty arose subsequent to the time of sale or the rendering of the service
exceptions: UNKNOWN — AS 9 para 9.3 states the treatment as what is 'more appropriate' and names no exception to it in the extracted text
common_mistakes: reversing or reducing the original revenue when a customer later becomes doubtful — AS 9 para 9.3 points to a separate provision instead
confusing this with the pre-existing postponement rule: postponement applies to doubt at the time of raising the claim, this applies to doubt arising after
netting the provision against revenue instead of keeping it separate

recognising revenue late on the basis that payment is by instalments — where there is no uncertainty as to ultimate collection, revenue is recognised at the time of sale or rendering of service even though payments are made by instalments
legal_references: UNKNOWN — statutory backing not extracted from any downloaded source in this pass
gst_references: NOT APPLICABLE — a provision for a doubtful receivable does not alter the GST already accounted on the supply; that is a separate determination
evidence_required: the date and document of original recognition
the event or document that raised the later doubt, with its date
the two dates must be distinguishable, or the rule cannot be selected
confidence_factors: weak when the document does not date the uncertainty, because the whole rule turns on before-versus-after
weak when original recognition cannot be located, so it is unknown whether revenue was ever recognised
REQUIRES HUMAN ACCOUNTANT when the uncertainty plausibly existed at the time of sale and only became visible later — AS 9 turns on when the uncertainty AROSE, and the documents rarely settle that
validation_checks: the originally recorded revenue amount is unchanged
a separate provision exists, and is not netted against revenue
the uncertainty is dated after the time of sale or the rendering of the service
examples: goods sold and revenue recognised in April; in September the customer enters difficulty — the April revenue stands, and a separate provision is made
counterexamples: a price escalation claim raised where the ability to assess ultimate collection with reasonable certainty is lacking at the time of raising the claim — revenue recognition is postponed to the extent of the uncertainty (para 9.2), and no revenue was recognised to provide against
a sale collected in instalments with no uncertainty as to ultimate collection — revenue is recognised at the time of sale, and no provision arises from the instalment terms alone
